macro_objective: Calculate baseline regional rainfall metrics via real-world measurements.

mls_units.title: Community Framework Layout & Container Securement
mls_units.macro_alignment: Sets up safe, approved collection points so the class can gather the rainfall data the baseline is calculated from.

tasks.action: Present the class goal of measuring local rainfall; show a reused plastic bottle cut and marked as a rain gauge.
In mixed pairs, sketch two possible gauge spots on the school grounds and note why each is open to the sky and safe to reach.
Hold a show-of-hands round to pick the two preferred spots, then take them to the Community_Governance_Body for approval.
With the educator present, help fix the approved gauges in place.

mls_units.title: Daily Rainfall Recording & Baseline Calculation
mls_units.macro_alignment: Turns 4 weeks of daily gauge readings in the class table into the baseline rainfall figures.

tasks.action: Recall from MLS-HYDRO-01: use the approved gauge spots and the blank class table. Each school morning, the pair on that day's rota reads each gauge, writes the millimetres in that day's row of the class table, then empties the gauge. Partners swap reader and recorder each turn, and the rota gives every pair a turn.
Each Friday, total the week's readings with the class in the totals row of the class table. Where a reading covers more than one day (after a weekend or holiday), write the number of days next to it.

In mixed groups, use the class table to work out the week's average daily rainfall: the week's total divided by the number of days the readings cover. Groups rotate who calculates and who checks each week.

On the last school day of week 4, work through the class table with the class to find the 4-week total and the average daily rainfall. Write these baseline figures at the top of the table with the dates they cover, then empty the gauges and bring them indoors.
